title: Year 6 fractions block
boundary: This block teaches fraction equivalence, ordering, operations and quantities, with fraction-as-division and familiar fraction–decimal–percentage connections. General decimal calculation, written decimal division and rounding remain in the separate decimals block. The accessible models are not themselves evidence of formal mastery.

lessons.title: Same amount, new pieces
lessons.goal: Keep the whole fixed and explain why splitting every part equally gives an equivalent fraction.

lessons.title: Make the fraction simpler
lessons.goal: Use a common factor to regroup equal pieces, and recognise when no common factor greater than 1 remains.

lessons.title: Across one whole
lessons.goal: Connect mixed numbers, improper fractions and positions on a number line.

lessons.title: Which is greater?
lessons.goal: Compare and order fractions, including amounts greater than one, using equivalence or benchmarks.

lessons.title: Combine equal-sized pieces
lessons.goal: Add fractions with different denominators by creating equal-sized fractional units.

lessons.title: Take away and find the gap
lessons.goal: Subtract unlike fractions using a shared unit, and interpret subtraction as removal or a difference.

lessons.title: Exchange a whole
lessons.goal: Add and subtract mixed numbers, including exchanging one whole into fractional pieces.

lessons.title: A fraction of a fraction
lessons.goal: Use an area model to find a fraction of a fraction, then connect the overlap to multiplication.

lessons.title: Share a fractional amount
lessons.goal: Share a proper fraction into equal groups while keeping the original whole as the reference.

lessons.title: Parts and the whole
lessons.goal: Find a fractional amount and reason backwards from a known fractional part to the whole.

lessons.title: One amount, three names
lessons.goal: Connect a fraction to a division, and recognise familiar fraction, decimal and percentage names for the same amount.

lessons.title: Choose a route
lessons.goal: Choose operations from the meaning of a problem, estimate the answer, and explain a connected solution.
